finding.title: The ask card's 'about CHF' is far below what Use API key then spends, and below the dialog's and plan card's figures for the same work
finding.what_the_person_sees: Card: 'Your API key can do the waiting work now: about CHF 0.10.' After Use API key the session spends CHF 0.65: CHF 0.24 on the two tasks that waited, the rest on two tasks the agent added under the same yes. For the same waiting work the Start dialog said 'about CHF 0.15' and the plan card 'About CHF 0.37 for the 2 tasks'. Second stop: card CHF 0.05, plan card CHF 0.15, dialog CHF 0.10.
finding.expected: The card's figure is within a factor of two of the real spend after Use API key, and the card, the dialog and the plan card give one figure for the same waiting work (C6L-3).
finding.evidence: Inbox API body 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 08:26. Your API key can do the waiting work now: about CHF 0.10.'; start-session-run-out 'Runs now on your API key until 08:26, about CHF 0.15; nothing passes this session's budget.'; ledger after the press: 60 rows, USD 0.818311 (task 16874e 0.212904, task 5d66a1 0.088728, added 07a838 0.395557, added 0ce1e8 0.108554). Files: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs-evidence/c24b.json, c24c.json.
finding.repro: Save both credentials, choose 'Subscription first, ask before API key', and have the subscription at its limit. Draft a 2-task plan and press Approve and start. Read the card, the Start dialog and the plan card. Press Use API key. Compare with Costs.
finding.suspected_cause: The card's estimate (credential-ask's estimate_usd_micro, priced with the Start check) seems to count only part of the waiting work. It has no margin for reviews and rework, and none for tasks the agent adds while the yes stands.

verdict.root_cause:
The ask card's figure is the closure in compose.ts that RouterTaskBilling's `ask` calls. For each waiting project it adds two things: `check.runnable` (ready tasks, priced by the planner), and the claimed or in_progress tasks at their raw stored figure, `(t.est_cost_usd_micro || t.budget_usd_micro || 500_000) - actual`. That second part was added in CS-8. Two gaps follow.
(1) The task that hit the stop is claimed when the card is filed, so it is priced at the plan's raw work-only guess. That guess has no review part. The Start dialog and the plan card price the same task with planEstimateUsdMicro / estimates.of, which add the review part (d1116-budget-all). This goes against the owner's binding answer of 2026-11-16 ("its estimate includes the reviews and fixes").
(2) It ignores `check.later`: the follower tasks that wait on the claimed task. A "Use API key" yes runs them in the same session (ADR 0120 §3: the waiting session goes on as the person's start, and promiseOf counts runnable + later).
The bench DB confirms this exactly. The first card's change_card.estimate_usd_micro = 126000, which equals the coder task's est_cost_usd_micro (126000); the tester task (est 207000) is not counted. The second card's 66000 equals the Bird walk coder's est_cost_usd_micro (66000); its tester (90000) is not counted.
The other two figures differ as well. The Start dialog's Use API key line (server.ts credentialAtStart) sums only `r.runnable`, so CHF 0.15 is the coder alone with its review part. The plan card prices every task with its review part: 0.15 + 0.22 = CHF 0.37. The result is three figures for one piece of waiting work. Real spend on the two waiting tasks was CHF 0.24 (0.212904 + 0.088728 USD), 2.4x the card's CHF 0.10. With the fix, the card would read about the plan card's 0.37, within a factor of two of 0.24 and also of the total 0.65.
The other CHF 0.41 went to two tasks the agent added during the run (D7, allowed by the owner). No up-front estimate can foresee them. That part is by design: the session budget still bounds it, and the explain line honestly says "for what waits now".
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:1811-1827 (ask closure: inFlight priced at raw est_cost_usd_micro at :1820; sum of check.runnable + inFlight only, no check.later, at :1826); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1567-1572 (Start dialog's Use API key figure: r.runnable only); packages/runtime/src/session/start-check.ts:142-160 (promiseOf, the figure both should use)
verdict.failing_test_idea: Add a composed case to packages/runtime/test/credential-ask-figure.test.ts using credWorld with no injected provider. The project has two tasks, B depending on A, with planner estimates whose review part is non-zero. Set policy subscription_then_ask, limit the subscription, start a session and call settleSessions. Then read three things at the person's boundary: the "Use your API key until 15:00?" card body from GET /inbox, the start-check's Use API key line from GET /projects/:id/start-check, and the plan card's per-task figures for the same tasks. Assert that the card's "about CHF N" equals the dialog's figure, and that both equal the A+B promise priced with the review part. Assert that it is more than A's raw est_cost_usd_micro alone. Today the card gives A's raw estimate only (as with 126000 vs the plan's 0.37) and the dialog gives A only.
verdict.notes:
C6L-3 (rated words) already names the three figures (card, runnable-only dialog, plan card per task) and asks for one figure per thing. This finding shows the root cause is more than words. The card leaves out the follower tasks the yes will run, and it prices the claimed task without its review part, so the money consent understates the waiting work by more than 2x on the real run. That is why I keep major; minor is also defensible, since the amounts are small and the session budget still caps everything.
The expectation that the card match spend that includes the agent-added tasks is too strong. That part is model and design (D7), not code.
Evidence checked in the read-only DB /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs/home/data/state.sqlite: the human_request change_card estimate_usd_micro values 126000 and 66000 match the task rows' est_cost_usd_micro exactly.
Also seen in c24b, not part of this finding: the request_blocking notification title says "until 07:26" while the card says "until 08:26", which looks like a UTC vs local time mix-up in the notification words.

finding.title: The ask card's notification gives the reset time in UTC, an hour off the card
finding.what_the_person_sees: Urgent notification: 'Use your API key until 07:26?' / 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 07:26. ...' The Inbox card, rows, bar and Settings all say 08:26 (the person's zone is Europe/Zurich). Same for the second stop: 07:01 against 08:01. The credential_switch notification in LC-C23 used the person's clock (08:28).
finding.expected: Every sentence uses the person's clock, never UTC (C5 CE-4).
finding.evidence: GET /notifications/recent: request_blocking at 06:47:11.532Z, title 'Use your API key until 07:26?'. Inbox card title 'Use your API key until 08:26?'. restingUntil 2026-11-17T07:26:44Z; config timezone Europe/Zurich. File: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs-evidence/c24b.json.
finding.repro: Set a person's zone other than UTC and choose ask. With the subscription at its limit, press Approve and start on a plan. Read the desktop notification (GET /notifications/recent).
finding.suspected_cause: The notification text for the ask card is built without the person's timezone (formatted in the daemon's process zone, UTC on the bench). The card's own words are built with the timezone.

verdict.root_cause: The finding is real. The suspected cause is slightly off: the time is not formatted in the daemon's process zone, it is hard-coded to UTC. The ask card's row stores only a placeholder `why`. Its title and body are computed when the card is shown, by askCard() in request-words.ts, from ctx.credentialAsk.timezone. The Inbox fills that context: views.ts:1059-1060 calls credentialAskFor(), which reads human.timezone at views.ts:1088. The notification path does not. compose.ts:3451 calls notifications.requestOpened(row, human.id, names), and producers.ts:187-190 calls requestWords(req, { projectName, taskTitle }) with no credentialAsk. So askCard (request-words.ts:1385-1394) passes no timezone, and askCardWords then calls stopWordsOf, then clockTime(), then validZone(undefined), which returns "UTC" (credential-wait.ts:231). The urgent request_blocking notification therefore always gives the reset in UTC, for any person whose zone is not UTC, on a real PC as well as on the bench. The credential_switch notification is right because compose.ts:3554 formats `until` with human.timezone itself. A smaller related point: askCard falls back to Date.now() for nowMs (request-words.ts:1394) instead of the clock, so near midnight the same-day check ("07:26" or "Tue 18 Nov, 07:26") can also differ from the card.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts:187 (requestWords without credentialAsk); packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:3451 (caller passes no zone); packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:1393-1394 (timezone omitted, nowMs falls back to Date.now()); packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:231 (no zone means "UTC")
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Let requestOpened(req, humanId, names, ctx?) take the same RequestWordsContext pieces the Inbox uses, and pass them to requestWords.
2. In compose's humanRequest.insert hook (compose.ts ~3436-3451), when the row's change_card.key is CREDENTIAL_ASK_KEY, build the context the way the Inbox does. Either export views.ts credentialAskFor (or a small shared helper in request-words / views) and call it, or at least pass { timezone: human.timezone, nowMs: Date.parse(card.filed_at) }. The notification then says what the card says, including the sessionWaits and goesOnAt words.
3. Close the trap: askCardWords/stopWordsOf should not fall back silently to UTC for a person-facing sentence. Either make timezone required on AskCardInput, or have askCard take nowMs from card.filed_at instead of Date.now().
4. Grep the siblings that render request words outside the Inbox: requestOpened, the email/Telegram channels (which reuse the same Notification), and any summary or chat path that calls requestWords for a credential:ask row. Give each the same context.
5. Update docs/maintainers notifications and credential docs as the module rule requires.

Real-daemon route case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, in the 'd1109-cred-engine' describe:

2. Put the subscription stand-in at its limit with a reset at 07:26Z.

4. Assert that the request_blocking notification's title equals the ask card's requestView title, "Use your API key until 08:26?", and that its body contains "until 08:26" and not "07:26".

Add a unit twin in packages/runtime/test/notifications-wiring.test.ts that drives the composed insert hook with a credential:ask row and a Europe/Zurich human, and asserts the notifier received 08:26. Run both with TZ unset and with TZ=Europe/Zurich: the fallback is hard-coded UTC, so it fails either way.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-engine (CE-7 ask card; the notification wiring in compose/producers)
verdict.notes: I reproduced it at 4cf11fd with a tsx script, /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-5/repro.ts, run with TZ=Europe/Zurich (process zone Europe/Zurich). requestOpened(askRow) gives "Use your API key until 07:26?" / "...at its limit until 07:26...". requestWords with credentialAsk.timezone=Europe/Zurich gives "08:26". finding.title: 'Waits for your answer ... The card is in the Inbox.' stays after the card is answered
finding.what_the_person_sees: After Wait (and also after Use API key), these still read 'Waits for your answer: use your API key? The card is in the Inbox. 1 task waits on other tasks. CHF 0.00.': the session page result, the Overview's Last result, the Inbox Updates and the session_ended notification. Meanwhile the Inbox says 'Nothing needs you.' The rows are right.
finding.expected: That sentence shows only while the card is open (C5 leftovers).
finding.repro: Do the same as L4-creds-4, then press Wait on the card. Open the session page and the Overview.
finding.suspected_cause: The stored session summary and the Update are written when the session ends, while the card is still open, and are not reworded after the answer.

verdict.root_cause: The session result is stored when the session ends, while the ask card is still open. So it carries the ask form 'Waits for your answer: use your API key? The card is in the Inbox.': credential-wait.ts:291-292, reached through askShown in executor.ts:1842 / 2131, stored by runner.ts:3906-3914 (outcome.credentialWait = waitSentence(...)). Three places re-read that stored text: the session page (server.ts:2139), the Overview's Last result and Read aloud (views.ts:426), and the Inbox Update (server.ts:2475). All three go through resultAfterWait (run-indicator.ts:60-67). That function returns the text unchanged unless it contains '; then your session goes on.' (line 66), so nothing re-checks the ask sentence after the card is answered (askCardOpen false). The C5 fix-up (FX-CE B1) applied askShown only to sentences written after the answer, never to results already stored. Its test (credential-ask-words.test.ts, 'after Wait...') checks only the second session. Reproduced on the composed stand-in: after Wait, with no open ask card, GET /sessions/:first, GET /projects/:id/summary lastSession.summary and the GET /inbox Update all still say 'The card is in the Inbox'. verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/run-indicator.ts:66 (resultAfterWait handles only the goes-on clause); stored at packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3906; read at packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:2139, server.ts:2475, views.ts:426; sentence at packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:292

In resultAfterWait, or a storedResultNow wrapper all readers use: if the text has the ask form and askCardOpen(store, sourceId, stopKey) is false, swap it for what is true now. After Wait: waitSentence of the plain wait (askShown's plain form), which then passes through the existing goes-on rule ('Waits until 08:01 (your subscription's limit); then your session goes on.'). After Use API key: a line saying the work went on with your API key, or the plain stop sentence. Keep the 3-line result rule. verdict.notes: Reproduced on the composed stand-in (cred-world, subscription_then_ask, subscription at its limit) through the daemon routes, both after Wait and after Use API key. One part of the finding is not a defect: the session_ended notification was sent at 06:55:20.414, after the card was filed at 06:55:20.389, so it was true when sent; a delivered notification is not reworded. After Use API key on the stand-in the continuation finishes at once, so the Overview shows the newer session's result; in the live run (c24c overviewRunning) the old result showed while the new session ran. That is the same defect on the Last result. Closest sibling leftover: C5L-15 (after Cancel, chat facts and the summary command read the stored result as written); it covers a different sentence, so no leftover names this one. finding.title: A 401 on the subscription is reported as a timeout or a failed call, not as a refused sign-in (bench caveat)
finding.what_the_person_sees: With the subscription first and nothing chosen, chat says 'I ran out of time before I could answer. Ask again, or ask for a shorter answer.' Planning says 'Planning failed: Claude did not answer (model call failed).' Task runs fail with 'Claude Code returned an error result: Authentication error · This may be a temporary network issue'. No 'Anthropic refused your Claude sign-in' card appears, and the next session picks the subscription again.
finding.expected: LC-C22: the refusal is read as a refusal, with one card and no second request to the subscription.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c31e-proxy/requests.jsonl ids 6, 12-14: POST /v1/messages?beta=true 401 for the bench subscription token. limits.subscription has no refusedAt; GET /inbox is empty. Caveat: the bench daemon passes this machine's remote-session proxy variables to Claude Code, so a real Claude Code's report may differ.
finding.repro: Save both credentials with an invalid subscription token and choose nothing. Ask chat a question and draft a plan.
finding.suspected_cause: ClaudeCodeProvider / the SDK driver does not map this authentication error result to provider_auth (refused).

verdict.root_cause:
The core claim holds: a refused subscription sign-in is never read as a refusal. The timeout part is a bench artefact. Agent SDK 0.3.304 sends three things in order: an assistant message with error "authentication_failed", then a result with is_error true, and then the iterator throws "Claude Code returned an error result: <text>". The SDK replaces Claude Code's non-zero exit with the result text. Both drivers turn authentication_failed into provider_auth only after the for-loop ends normally, and their catch blocks ignore what the loop had already seen.

(1) Chat and planning, ClaudeCodeProvider. packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:184 runs errorFromSdk only after the loop. `sdkError` and `rejected` are declared inside the try, so the catch at :195-206 cannot see them. It yields code provider_error, "Claude Code could not answer: ...". routed.ts:287 then sees no provider_auth, so it never calls refuse(): no refusedAt, no card, and the next call goes to the subscription again.

(2) Task runs, SdkAgentDriver. packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:586-604 is skipped when the iterator throws. The catch at :606-626 sets error = {code:"internal", message:"Claude Code returned an error result: ..."}. That overwrites even a correct provider_auth from the result handler at :487. The result-text check is weak anyway: REFUSED_TEXT in usage-limit.ts matches "authentication_error" but not "Authentication error ·". The c31 daemon.log shows exactly this catch line six times ("sdk run failed ... Claude Code returned an error result: Authentication error · ..."), so the tasks went to Failed.

I reproduced it at the provider boundary (/tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-9/probe.mts). With the same events and a normal end, ClaudeCodeProvider yields provider_auth. With the SDK's throw after them, it yields provider_error.

Bench artefact: chat's "I ran out of time before I could answer", and the ~60 s per planning call / ~3 min per task run, come from this machine's CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE reaching Claude Code. In the 0.3.304 binary, Z4t() returns CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE, which selects the "Authentication error · This may be a temporary network issue" branch. LC-C22, run with a clean environment, gives "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid." in 6 s, and chat says "I could not answer (model call failed)". It is still not a refusal. So only the wording and timing differ; the defect stands.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:195 (catch ignores sdkError; mapping only at :184); packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:606 (catch overwrites with "internal"; mapping only at :586-604 and :487)
verdict.fix_sketch:
claude-code.ts: hoist `sdkError` and `rejected` above the try. In the catch, when the request was not aborted and sdkError (or rejected) is set, yield errorFromSdk(sdkError.kind, sdkError.text, rejected) instead of the generic provider_error. The same goes for an is_error result seen before the throw.

sdk.ts: move the failedTurn mapping (usage limit, then refusal kind) into a helper. Call it after a normal loop end, and also in the catch when the throw is not a ForerunnerError (not a timeout, kill, budget or withheld stop). Do not overwrite an `error` already set to provider_auth or provider_usage_limit by the result handler. A thrown "Claude Code returned an error result" after a mapped error keeps the mapped one.

Optionally widen REFUSED_TEXT to cover "Authentication error ·" and "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401". The kind is the main signal, though.

The same fix probably uncovers CE-5's billing_error and rate_limit usage-limit path on the real SDK, which is hidden by the same throw. Change the fake query in the existing tests to throw after the result, the way 0.3.304 does. Fix it once, together with L4-creds-10, which is the same defect.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
This tests at the person's boundary, through the composed or real daemon. Setup: the subscription saved first, an API key second, nothing chosen. The scripted Claude Code (the queryImpl/query test seam) yields three things, as Agent SDK 0.3.304 does: assistant {error:'authentication_failed', text 'Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid.'}, then result {is_error:true}, then a throw of Error('Claude Code returned an error result: ...').

Steps: ask chat a question, then draft a plan, then Start a ready task.

Expected:
- limits.subscription.refusedAt is set.
- GET /inbox has exactly one 'Anthropic refused your Claude sign-in' card ('The sign-in has expired or was signed out. ...').
- Chat gives the hold reply, not 'model call failed' or 'ran out of time'.
- Planning and the task wait for a new sign-in; the task is not Failed and there is no failed-task card.
- Settings shows the subscription as Refused.
- The scripted query is called for the subscription exactly once in total.

Today: provider_error/internal, no refusedAt, an empty Inbox for chat and planning, a Failed task card, and a second call to the subscription.

Unit-level companions: ClaudeCodeProvider.stream yields code provider_auth, and SdkAgentDriver.run returns error.code provider_auth, both with the throwing fake.
verdict.notes:
No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names it. It is the same defect as live-4 finding L4-creds-10 (LC-C22, major, clean environment, real API 401); the two should be fixed and tracked as one. I agree with the claim but not the severity: I rate it major, not minor. Reason: an expired or invalid subscription sign-in makes every task Failed instead of waiting, chat and planning fail with raw errors, and nothing tells the person to save a new sign-in. That goes against owner decision D5c, which says a refusal follows the run-out policy and tells the person.

Evidence in c31e:
- requests.jsonl ids 6 and 12-14 are POST /v1/messages 401s answered locally by the logging proxy (local:true), not by the bench stand-in.
- daemon.log shows 'billing source picked ... kind subscription driver sdk' and then 'intake: the planning call ended error: model call failed'.
- In c31, all six task runs ended in sdk.ts's catch log line.
- The proxy's ws/ca-cert lines (ids 2-5, 8-11) are the CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE contamination named in the caveat.

Probe: /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-9/probe.mts, run with node --experimental-transform-types from the worktree.

finding.title: Two notifications for one refused key; the refusal's says 'Answer it in the Inbox' though there is nothing to answer
finding.what_the_person_sees: First, urgent: 'Anthropic refused your API key' / '... until then the work waits. Answer it in the Inbox.' Then: 'Field notes: Waits for a new API key: save one in…' / 'CHF 0.00. Open the session for the details.' (the title is cut). The card has no options, only Save a new key.
finding.expected: One notification per refusal that says to save a new key.
finding.suspected_cause: The notify words add 'Answer it in the Inbox' to every request_blocking notification. The session_ended notification is sent as well.

verdict.root_cause:
Two separate code paths each send a notification, and neither knows about the other.

(1) Wrong instruction in the urgent notification. `fileRefusedCard` (session/credential-wait.ts:647-667) files the refused card as kind "info" with `options: []`. Its words (request-words.ts:1433-1468) have `choices: []`, `reply: "none"` and one link, "Save a new key", to /setup. compose's humanRequest.insert hook (compose.ts:3434-3452) sends `notifications.requestOpened` for every card. `requestOpened` (notifications/producers.ts:198) always adds "Answer it in the Inbox." and links to /inbox, so a card with nothing to answer is told as one to answer. The hook also passes only the project and task names, not the refusal context that only the Inbox view supplies (views.ts:1057, credentialRefusedFor). So `refusedCredentialCard` falls back to category null and rule "wait". The notification then says "Anthropic did not accept it. ... until then the work waits." while the card says "The key is not valid or was deleted. ...". By the same code path, under a "next" policy the notification would say the work waits while the other credential takes it (read in the code, not reproduced).

(2) A second notification that repeats the card. The runner leaves out of `news` only what open cards of the project say about their tasks. `openCards` is queried by project_id (runner.ts:3812-3824), and `told` is {tasks: carded, docker, plan} (runner.ts:3986-3990). The refused card has project_id and task_id null, so it is never counted. The "credential wait" result builder (result.ts:301-303) adds 'Waits for a new API key: save one in Settings; then your session goes on.' with no check against an open card. `isNewsLine` counts it as news, so `sessionEndIsNews` (producers.ts:305) is true and compose (compose.ts:3886-3889) sends a session_ended notification. The same lines also post an Inbox Update. `titled`/`fit` then cuts that one sentence to 'Field notes: Waits for a new API key: save one in…', leaving 'CHF 0.00. Open the session for the details.' as the body.

This breaks: design §4.3 and §5.10 (the person hears once; one place per fact), §5.1 and §5.8 (say what to do), §5.9 (no promise the code does not keep), notifications.md "Hearing once" ("a session whose only news is its cards sends nothing of its own"), and the owner's D5 ('also tells the person (what was refused, how to fix it)'; 'We don't need notifications like that' for waiting work).

Reproduced on the stand-in at 4cf11fd: bench-api with --api-key refused, one ready task. GET start-check showed blocked:null, so the Start dialog's Start is enabled before any refusal is known. One POST /sessions, as Start sends it, gave two notifications 24 ms apart:
- request_blocking (urgent): 'Anthropic refused your API key' / 'Anthropic did not accept it. Save a new one in Settings; until then the work waits. Answer it in the Inbox.' (link /inbox)
- session_ended: 'Field notes: Waits for a new API key: save one in…' / 'CHF 0.00. Open the session for the details.'

finding.title: Chat's hold reply promises it can start tasks while nothing can start
finding.what_the_person_sees: Chat: 'Anthropic refused your API key, so I have not answered. I can still add, move and start tasks.' At the same time the Start dialog says 'Nothing can run until you save a new API key in Settings.' and Start is disabled.
finding.expected: The reply names what still works and what to do (save a new key).
finding.repro: With only the refused key, ask chat a question, then open Start.

verdict.root_cause: The hold reply is written by code, not by the model: a held chat question makes no model call. `chatHoldReply` (packages/runtime/src/session/credential-words.ts:345-350) uses one template for every stop and always ends with "I can still add, move and start tasks." It does not look at the wait's reason, and it never says what to do. The sentence was written for the subscription-limit case (run C plan CE-9; design §3.9 States; the unit test at packages/runtime/test/credential-refusal.test.ts:255-258). In that case Start stays on, because `waits.now` returns `startable` with "Start at 15:40" whenever `reason !== "refused"` (packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:4690-4700). A refused key gets no `startable`, so `startBlocked` (packages/runtime/src/daemon/start-blocked.ts:84-101) turns Start off with "Nothing can run until you save a new API key in Settings." The refused case reuses the limit template unchanged. The reply's "start" also has no backing in chat itself. Chat's own `startBlocked` port (compose.ts:4809-4833) never passes the credential wait, even though its comment at :4808 says it "refuses in words what the Start dialog refuses". So "start a session" in chat is read back, the person says yes, and chat replies "Started a session ..." while that session ends at once to wait and runs nothing.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/credential-words.ts:345 (the sentence at :349); called at packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1355 (question held before any call) and :2236 (held after the first 401); the related chat start port is at packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:4809-4833
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Make `chatHoldReply` depend on the reason. For a refusal: "Anthropic refused your API key, so I have not answered. Save a new key in Settings; until then I can still add and change tasks." For a refused subscription, the same sentence with "Sign in again in Settings". For a limit, share or monthly cap, mention starting only where a start is actually kept: "... I can still add and change tasks; a Start now runs at 15:40." Optionally put the save link on the reply view the way `oneOff` is carried, so chat shows "Save a new key" like the header and the Start dialog.
2. Sibling fix: have chat's `startBlocked` port in compose.ts pass the refused credential wait, as the dialog's check does at server.ts:1655. Then "start a session" in chat answers "Nothing can run until you save a new API key in Settings." instead of a read-back and "Started a session".
3. Update design §3.9 States (core-experience.md:252), user-guide.md:1082, docs/maintainers/runtime.md, and the unit expectation in credential-refusal.test.ts.
verdict.failing_test_idea: On the composed runtime (packages/runtime/test/chat-credential-hold.test.ts, or a refused-key case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts): policy key_only, and the only credential is a refused API key. In the same test, assert that GET /projects/:id/start-check gives blocked.sentence === "Nothing can run until you save a new API key in Settings." with no `startable`, so the two screens agree. Add a second case: chat "start a session" gets the dialog's sentence, not "Start a session on ... ?". A ChatTab UI test should assert the visible reply text. verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-engine (owns credential-words.ts chatHoldReply and the agent.ts hold, item CE-9); d1109-cred-screens if the reply gets a "Save a new key" link
verdict.notes:

A plan-card task line 'Press Start and the work starts then.' next to 'Approve and start: ... starts working on them now'. And beside every waiting Cancel: 'Nothing starts when Claude is back; its tasks wait for your Start.' right after 'waiting until 08:26, then it goes on' (it explains Cancel but reads as a contradiction).

finding.evidence: GET /notifications/recent in /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs-evidence/c24c.json and c24e.json; plan cards in c24b.json; /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs/steps/13-c24-inbox-ask-card.png

verdict.root_cause:
Three of the four sub-claims come from the code. I reproduced the two notification texts exactly by running `sessionEnded` from the 4cf11fd checkout under tsx (script at /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-7/repro.ts).

(1) "and 2 more and 1 more": the session result's first line is built by `namesOf` (packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts:39-44). In the evidence it reads 'Did 4 tasks: "Build the quote…", "Check the page's…", "Make the quote selection test…" and 1 more.' The title is too long for 60 characters, so `fit()` in packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts:124-145 rebuilds the quoted list with fewer names. It writes `nameList(names.slice(0, keep), names.length - keep)` and then appends `text.slice(end)`, the text after the last quote. That tail still holds the old " and 1 more", so both counts are printed. Reproduced output: 'Quote page: did 4 tasks: "Build the…" and 2 more and 1 more'. Any session that finishes four or more tasks with long titles hits this.

(2) Doubled pointer: under 'ask', `waitSentence` (packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:292) writes "Waits for your answer: use your API key? The card is in the Inbox.". `splitResult` (producers.ts:262-279) puts the question in the title and starts the body with "The card is in the Inbox.". `sessionEnded` (producers.ts:321-329) then sets `asks` because a news line mentions "Inbox", and `bodyOf` adds "Answer it in the Inbox." on top. Reproduced output: "The card is in the Inbox. 1 task waits on other tasks. CHF 0.00. Answer it in the Inbox." Without `news`, the same body ends in "Open the session for the details.", which is still two pointers.

(3) Plan-card line: the credential chooser in compose.ts:4180-4185 gives every resting credential the line from `waitThenStartSentence` (credential-wait.ts:342-350). That line ends with the constant PRESS_START_THEN (credential-wait.ts:320) and is written for New task. The plan card has no Start button; its button is "Approve and start". In c24b, pressing it started the session at once, which then waited ("waiting until 08:26, then it goes on") and filed the ask card. So "Press Start" names a button that is not on the card, and "the work starts then" contradicts what the button does. Leftover C6L-8 already names this.

(4) The text next to Cancel is not a defect in the app as rendered. It is `CANCEL_WAIT_EXPLAIN` (packages/runtime/src/daemon/run-wait-words.ts:8-9), shown by `CancelWait` (apps/ui/src/shell/RunIndicator.tsx:219-229). This is the intended form from d1109-run-visible V-2/V-5, and the owner decided on "Waiting until 15:40, then it goes on, with Cancel". In screenshot 13 it sits right-aligned and directly against the Cancel button, far from "waiting until 08:26, then it goes on". It only reads as a contradiction in the flattened text dump. At most it is a wording nit, because the sentence does not name Cancel.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts:136-141 (fit: tail after the list keeps the old "and N more"); packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts:321-329 (sessionEnded adds "Answer it in the Inbox." to a body that already says "The card is in the Inbox."); packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:292 (the wait sentence carries its own pointer); packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:4184 with packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:320,342-350 (the plan card gets New task's "Press Start" line); apps/ui/src/shell/RunIndicator.tsx:219-229 with packages/runtime/src/daemon/run-wait-words.ts:8-9 (the text beside Cancel; designed)
verdict.fix_sketch:
(1) In producers.ts `fit()`: when the listed names are followed by /^ and (\d+) more/ in `text.slice(end)`, add that number to the dropped count (`names.length - keep + n`) and remove the match from the tail. One count then remains: '"Build the…" and 3 more'. Do the same in any other caller that rebuilds a list from `quotedNames`.

(2) In `sessionEnded`: when `first` or `rest` already has an Inbox pointer, drop the sentence "The card is in the Inbox." from `rest` and keep the one action. Alternatively, keep the sentence and pass no action. Either way the body points to the Inbox once.

(3) Give the chooser line a context: `waitThenStartSentence(wait, {..., on: "plan" | "new_task"})`. On the plan card it should name the card's own button. Under 'then wait': "Waits until 08:26 (your subscription's limit); Approve and start keeps it for then." Under 'ask': "...; Approve and start asks before your API key is used." New task keeps "Press Start...". This is C6L-8.

(4) Optional: make the text beside Cancel name the button, for example "Cancel: nothing starts when Claude is back; its tasks wait for your Start." The owner-decided indicator itself stays as it is.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
At the daemon boundary, with the composed real daemon and the stand-in provider, in packages/runtime/test/notifications-voice.test.ts or notifications-wiring.test.ts:

(a) A session finishes 4 tasks with titles of 40 or more characters. GET /notifications/recent: the session_ended title matches /and \d+ more/ exactly once and never /more and \d+ more/. Expected: 'Quote page: did 4 tasks: "Build the…" and 3 more'. This fails today with "and 2 more and 1 more".

A task's runs-on line must not contain "Press Start", because the card's only start button is "Approve and start". It must name "Approve and start" or say what that button does.
verdict.area_hint: Small fix area "notification-words" for (1) and (2): packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts fit/sessionEnded, and the runner's news filter for the ask-wait line. No run C area owns producers.ts. (3) belongs to d1109-cred-screens: the plan card's chooser line, compose.ts:4184 and credential-wait.ts waitThenStartSentence. Answer it in the Inbox.": real, reproduced exactly. (3) plan card "Press Start and the work starts then." beside "Approve and start: ... starts working on them now": real, and C6L-8 already names it. finding.suspected_cause: Agent SDK 0.3.304 replaces Claude Code's exit error with a thrown 'Claude Code returned an error result: <text>' after it has yielded the assistant error and the error result. packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts (the refusal mapping after the for-loop, around lines 586-604; catch around 606) and packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts (mapping around lines 182-186; catch at 195) only map authentication_failed and the 401 result text when the loop ends normally. Their catch blocks make the throw 'internal' or 'provider_error'. The tests' fake query ends the stream normally. The same throw probably hides Claude Code's billing_error/rate_limit (the subscription's usage limit, CE-5) on the real SDK.

verdict.root_cause:
Agent SDK 0.3.304's Query.readMessages queues every message first: the assistant error (error:"authentication_failed") and the result (is_error:true, result "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 ..."). When Claude Code then exits non-zero, it fails the input stream with `Error("Claude Code returned an error result: <result text>")`. In the bundled sdk.mjs, `lastErrorResultText` is set for any is_error result, so this replaces the exit error, and iterator.next() rejects after the last message. Forerunner's two consumers only read a refusal correctly when the loop ends normally.
(1) SDK driver, packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts. handle() does read the result as provider_auth (lines 482-490, since isClaudeCodeRefusal(null, said) matches "API Error: 401"). The for-loop at 572-581 then throws, so the post-loop sdkError mapping (usage limit, then authentication_failed, 583-605) never runs. The catch at 606-632 overwrites `error` with code "internal" (the thrown Error is not a ForerunnerError) and logs "sdk run failed". That is exactly the daemon.log line.
(2) Chat provider, packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts. The post-loop errorFromSdk mapping (182-186) is skipped. The catch at 195-207 yields provider_error "Claude Code could not answer: Claude Code returned an error result: ...".

finding.title: Chat's one-off 'Use API key' keeps the question twice in the conversation (C6L-6)
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'What should I do next here?', then 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 10:59, so I have not answered. I can still add, move and start tasks.', then 'What should I do next here?' again, then the answer. The question is still there twice after a reload.
finding.expected: One press answers the held question in place, so the question shows once (C6L-6).
finding.evidence: c25.json b.questionShown = 2 and b.questionShownAfterReload = 2. c25-proxy/bodies/5-req.json: the one-off request's messages hold the question twice, with the hold reply between as the assistant turn. Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c25/steps/12-c25-b-chat-after-reload.png.

verdict.root_cause: The one-off press is a brand-new chat turn carrying the same text, not an answer to the held turn. (1) apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:311 handles the press as `send(t.said, { oneOff: true })`, which also draws a second person bubble. (2) packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1082-1088 reads `earlier`, which already holds the held turn, then writes a new `chat.human` for every request; oneOffSwitch does not change this, so the transcript and conversation view hold the question twice, also after a reload. (3) The held turn was stored as an ordinary turn whose reply is the hold reply (agent.ts:1349-1373, notice:true with oneOff). (4) historyMessages (packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:374-401, replyInHistory at 354) does not skip notice or hold replies, and agent.ts:1605-1607 passes `earlier` in whole. So the model gets: user question, assistant "so I have not answered", user question again. The proxy body /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c25-proxy/bodies/5-req.json shows exactly this. C6L-6's description as "a display duplicate" is wrong: the extra line is stored and sent to the model. The answer was correct and booked once on the key, so the harm is a visible duplicate that survives a reload plus a few tokens of misleading model context. That makes it minor, not major.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:311; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1082-1088 (chat.human written for the one-off too), agent.ts:1349-1373 (held turn stored), agent.ts:1605-1607 + packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:374-401 (hold reply goes into the model history)

The live answer renders under that turn with no second person bubble. (2) Daemon: add `heldTurn` to the chat request (api-types.ts, server.ts:2684/2713, agent.ts). When the newest turn in `earlier` is that held turn and its reply is a hold reply with the one-off: write no new chat.human; write the answer as a chat.reply for the held turn's transcriptId, so readTranscript keeps it in place of the hold reply; build the model history from `earlier` without that held turn, so the question goes to the model once. (3) Separately, historyMessages skips hold replies (a notice with oneOff), since the model never wrote them. (4) The fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts) does the same.

finding.what_the_person_sees: After three chat answers on the key (CHF 0.002), Total spend reads 'less than CHF 0.01' and By model reads 'less than CHF 0.01', but By credential reads 'Your API key: CHF 0.00'. That line reads as if nothing was charged to the key.

finding.title: Merge pressed ~1 s after a push answers 'Merging #62.', then refuses 4 s later
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Merging #62.' then the row reads '#62 changed after the review ...'. Nothing is merged.
finding.repro: With the Overview open, push a commit to an accepted PR's branch, then press Merge within ~1 s.
finding.suspected_cause: GitHub's pull list was probably stale ~1 s after the push. A press at normal person speed was not retested.

verdict.root_cause: The press checks for a moved head before it answers, but it compares the reviewed commit only with the head that GitHub's pull-request endpoints report. GitHub updates a pull request's head.sha in the background after a push, so for a moment after the push those endpoints still show the old head. The branch ref itself moves as soon as the push returns. On a pull request whose task builds on nothing gone, the press's only head check is pull-requests.ts:751-760. It reads `listed.find(...).head.sha` from the GET /pulls?state=open it just made (read() -> readView, pull-requests.ts:335). When that head equals reviewed_head_sha it does `continue` at line 757 and never calls headMovedNow. If the listing did have the new head, headMovedNow reads getPullRequest again (merge.ts:2094-2100, `moved = now?.head.sha || head`), which can be just as stale, and then returns null. Either way the press goes on to approveInOrder and answers {state: "queued", "Merging #62."}. The background merge step reads getPullRequest again (merge.ts:363/378). By then GitHub has the new head, so it settles the record head_moved and the row shows the red line. Nowhere does the press read the branch ref (host.getBranchHead, already in the GitHost port). Timeline from the evidence: push 200 at 09:53:01.691Z. The press was clicked straight after it returned (press.cjs clicks right after act()); the ~1 s in the finding is how long the answer took, not the gap. The answer came at about 09:53:02.72. The daemon log has 'merge record ... left_to_you head_moved' at 09:53:04.256Z, and the screenshot taken just after the answer already shows '#62 is not merged yet: the row below says why.' So the refusal came about 1.5 s after the answer, not 4 s. Nothing wrong can merge: the final PUT pins sha (merge.ts:550). The harm is one contradicting answer.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:751-760 (head check on the listing's head.sha, skip at 757); packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:2094-2100 (headMovedNow re-reads getPullRequest, which lags the same way)
verdict.fix_sketch: Judge the press against the branch ref, which the push itself moves at once, not against the pull request's head as GitHub reports it. In ProjectPullRequests.merge (pull-requests.ts:751-760), for each chain task with a reviewed_head_sha, read `host.getBranchHead(ref, listedPr.head.ref)`. Take that head when it differs from the listing's head.sha, and call headMovedNow whenever either one differs from the reviewed commit. In headMovedNow (merge.ts:2094-2100), do not let a getPullRequest head equal to the reviewed commit override a newer head passed in from the branch read. Use the branch head when it is not the reviewed one, so that keepsOwnChange (GitHub's Update branch) and the rebuilt-by-Forerunner case still decide as they do today. This costs one extra GET per chain task per press. Leave the merge step's sha-pinned PUT as it is.
verdict.failing_test_idea: In packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts (chainWorld), plus a real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts: give the fake git host a 'pull head lag' option, so a push moves refs/heads/<branch> at once but the pull request's head.sha keeps the old commit until a later read or clock tick. Today syncPullsForBranch in testenv/src/githost/ops.ts:296 updates it in the same step as the push, which is why the existing 'L3-github-3: Merge pressed...' case passes at the base. Run a task to accepted, push a commit to its branch with the lag on, then at once press Merge through POST /projects/:id/pull-requests/:n/merge, as the Overview's Merge does. Expect {state: 'refused', sentence: '#N changed after the review: look at the new commits, ...'}, nothing merged, the record left_to_you/head_moved and one card. At the base it answers {state: 'queued', sentence: 'Merging #N.'} and refuses afterwards.
verdict.area_hint: l3-merge (run L3's merge area, which owned L3-github-3 and the press-time head check; no run C d1109-* area owns merge)
verdict.notes: This does not reproduce on the stand-in bench: FakeGitHost moves a pull request's head in the same step as the push, and the existing L3-github-3 unit case passes at 4cf11fd (run under flock). The code still explains the live result: the press trusts only pull-request heads, which lag a push on real GitHub. Corrections to the finding: the press came milliseconds after the push's 200, not about 1 s after (1032 ms was the answer's latency), and the row turned red about 1.5 s after the answer (log at 09:53:04.256Z; the screenshot just after the answer already shows it), not 4 s. A person who pushes and then comes to the app will rarely be this fast, and nothing can be merged by mistake (the merge PUT pins the sha), so it stays minor: it is a race at machine speed and the cost is one contradicting answer. LL-2 in leftovers-L3.json is a sibling (a check failed or the PR stopped merging cleanly after the last look, and the press still says 'Merging #N.' first). It assumes head moves are already said at once, so it does not name this case.

finding.title: Chat says 'Answered with your Claude subscription' under a reply that says it could not answer
finding.what_the_person_sees: In chat, with the API key at its limit, preset 'API key first, then subscription', and a subscription that Anthropic does not accept, the reply reads: 'I could not answer (model call failed).' Under it: [Think it through] 'Thinks longer on this model: about 30 seconds, at most CHF 0.03.' and the footer 'Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 11:57.'
finding.expected: No 'Answered with ...' note when nothing answered. The note appears once, under the first answer the subscription really gives. A failed answer says why and what to do (design section 5), and no paid 'Think it through' is offered on the credential that just failed.
finding.evidence: c26.json: chatProxyReqs shows 4 POST /v1/messages?beta=true with the subscription token, all 401; chatApiReqs is [] (no call on the key); chatFooters is ['Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 11:57.']. Daemon log at 10:20:21.758Z: 'ERROR [agent-loop] run failed {error: "model call failed"}'. Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/12-c26-chat-question.png.
finding.repro: On a bench like c26: the key is resting (restingUntil set), the preset is key_then_subscription, and the subscription is one Anthropic refuses (the bench's token). Ask any chat question.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts around l.1378-1390 builds switchNote before the model call, from the hold check (credHold.answersOn), and marks the stop as noted. Around l.2306 it is used as the footer whatever the call's outcome. The 'noted' mark then also keeps the note off the first real answer.

verdict.root_cause: The CE-9 note comes from the hold check made before the model call, and the outcome of the call never gates it. At agent.ts:1378-1387, credentialHold() reports not held with answersOn=subscription because the key is resting. switchNote is built from that prediction. At :1388-1391 the stop goes into conv.notedStops at once, before any model call. At :2296-2307 the footer is `(stopped ? … : deep ? … : null) ?? switchNote ?? fixFooter`, and nothing there checks result.outcome. So when the call fails, the note "Answered with your Claude subscription: …" still sits under "I could not answer (model call failed).". The stop is already marked as noted, so the first answer the subscription really gives in this conversation gets no note. Separately, the Think it through closer at :2274-2292 needs only `result && longerFigures && !heldAfter && results.length===0`. It never checks result.outcome === "completed", so a failed call still gets the paid offer. A second cause explains why the reply says "model call failed" and not a refusal or hold reply. Agent SDK 0.3.304 throws "Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 …" from the iterator. claude-code.ts:195-204 catches it as provider_error and never runs isClaudeCodeRefusal on it. RoutedProvider therefore never marks the subscription refused, the loop throws provider_error "model call failed" (loop.ts:842), and agent.ts:2226-2239 never re-checks the hold, because provider_error is not in CREDENTIAL_HOLD_CODES.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1380 (switchNote built and noted at :1388-1391 before the call); agent.ts:2306 (footer uses switchNote whatever the outcome); agent.ts:2274 (closer offered under a failed call); contributing: packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:200 (thrown 401 result text mapped to provider_error)
verdict.fix_sketch: In agent.ts, keep switchNote as a candidate before the call, but do not add the stop to conv.notedStops there. After the run, use the note as the footer only if a model answer was really given: result?.outcome === "completed" (or deep.result completed), !stopped and !heldAfter. Only then add stopNoted to notedStops. A better version takes the credential from the call's own billing (message_end billing.sourceId and kind, or the ledger row) and not from the pre-call prediction, so a switch inside the call is named correctly. Add `result.outcome === "completed"` to the closer condition at :2274, so no Think it through appears under a failure. For the reply itself, the catch in claude-code.ts:195 should run isClaudeCodeRefusal(null, errorMessage(e)) and give provider_auth. Do the same in the sdk.ts catch at about :606 for task runs. RoutedProvider then marks the subscription refused, files the one card and tries the next source. Chat then gets the hold or refusal reply through CREDENTIAL_HOLD_CODES and not "I could not answer (model call failed)." The general wording of chat failures is C3L-7.
verdict.failing_test_idea: A composed-runtime test through POST /chat, set up like packages/runtime/test/billing-order.test.ts (fetchImpl Messages API stand-in plus the sdkQuery Claude Code stand-in). Set credential_policy to key_then_subscription. The API answers 400 "You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-10-31 at 11:00 UTC." Turn 1: the key rests and Claude Code answers. Then the sdkQuery stand-in throws Error("Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."). Turn 2 must have no footer matching /^Answered with/, and its chat.reply event must have no closer. Then Claude Code answers again (a new token is saved). Turn 3's footer must be "Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 12:00." finding.title: The session page shows two clocks: the computer's beside the person's zone
finding.what_the_person_sees: The header reads 'Moss notes · session at 10:19' and the log times read '10:19'. Beside them: 'Your subscription took over at 11:19 (your API key's limit)' and 'your API key is at its limit until 11:57'. The Sessions list row reads '10:19 · under a minute'.

Every desktop time helper in apps/ui/src/lib/time.ts calls toLocaleTimeString/toLocaleDateString("en-GB", HH_MM) and never passes a timeZone, so it uses the browser's zone: formatTime :49-54, formatClock :23-30 (its "today" test at :28 is also the browser's day), formatDateTime :11-16, formatDate and formatDayMonth :33-46. The file's own header (:2-4) and formatClock's comment (:18-21) say they match "the daemon's own sentences ... clockTime". They do not. The daemon's clockTime (packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:203-228) formats with timeZone = human.timezone, and the session result line uses it (packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:2099-2100, credential-policy-view.ts:441 resultSwitchLine), as do the log line "your API key is at its limit until 11:57" and every other "until/at HH:MM" sentence. On the session page, the title (apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx:70-75 startedAtWords -> formatTime, title built at :379) and each log row (:691 formatTime(e.at)) are in the browser's zone. The daemon's sentences on the same page are in the person's zone. The Sessions row (apps/ui/src/pages/project/SessionsTab.tsx:31 formatClock) and FilesTab.tsx:20-22 use the browser's zone too. The evidence matches exactly. The c26 config has timezone Europe/Zurich (home/config/config.json:5). The bench ran at 10:16-10:25 UTC and the browser was in UTC. So one instant (10:19Z) reads "session at 10:19" and "10:19" in the log, but "took over at 11:19" (UTC+1) beside them, and the reset "until 11:57" is 10:57Z. I reproduced it: under TZ=UTC, toLocaleTimeString of 2026-11-17T10:19:30Z gives 10:19, and Intl with Europe/Zurich gives 11:19. The run was on the stand-in (provider bench-api, live false), so it reproduces without the real model. The UI can already read the person's zone from GET /me (server.ts:850-856, timezone), but lib/time.ts never uses it. The mobile helpers take a zone, but the store passes deviceTimezone() (apps/ui/src/mobile/store.tsx:373), so the phone has the same gap.

(3) Route FilesTab.tsx:20-22 through formatClock instead of its own toLocaleTimeString. (4) Mobile: seed env.timezone from /me.timezone instead of deviceTimezone() (store.tsx:373). finding.evidence: In c26 the proxy at anthropicApiBase logged 0 requests during the task run (10:19:35-10:19:38) and 4 during the chat turn (10:20:19). The run's 401 reads 'OAuth access token is invalid', which is the real API's wording; the proxy answers 'Invalid bearer token'. The same happened in c22: its run (09:00:57-09:01:03) has no proxy entry, and the proxy's subscription entries come only from chat at 09:01:41 (/tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22-proxy/requests.jsonl).

verdict.root_cause: The configured `anthropicApiBase` never reaches the Agent SDK driver that runs a task on the subscription. `SdkAgentDriver.run` only sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from `req.baseURL` (sdk.ts:62, :523), and no caller sets that field. The executor's one SDK call (executor.ts:1549-1580) passes token, credential, model, prompt, cwd, tools and similar fields, plus `env` only when Headroom's `sessionContext.sdkEnv` is set. It never passes a baseURL. `SdkExecutorDeps` (executor.ts:363-378) has no base field. compose.ts builds the driver (2119-2125) and the executor's `sdk` deps (2602-2608) without `config.anthropicApiBase`. compose.ts passes the address only to the per-call providers: `ClaudeCodeProvider` (1869), which serves chat, planning and reviews on the subscription, and `AnthropicMessagesProvider` (1882), which serves the key. That is why chat on the subscription went through the gateway and the subscription task run did not. The evidence agrees with the code. In c26 (config.json anthropicApiBase http://127.0.0.1:49048) the daemon picked the subscription with driver "sdk" at 10:19:34.986. The run failed at 10:19:38.841 with Claude Code's "401 OAuth access token is invalid", which is the real API's wording; the proxy would have answered "Invalid bearer token" locally (proxy.mjs:136). The proxy log has only the 4 chat requests at 10:20:19-20. c22 shows the same pattern: the SDK run failed at 09:01:04 with no proxy entry, and the chat entries came at 09:01:41. Then sdk.ts:523 uses `req.baseURL ?? this.deps.baseURL`, so every SDK run gets it, task runs and any later SDK caller included. finding.title: Costs lists a model named '<synthetic>'
finding.what_the_person_sees: After a failed run on the subscription, the project's Costs page lists under By model: '<synthetic> · 1 · — · — · CHF 0.00'.
finding.expected: No internal marker shown as a model name. Book the run under the model it asked for, or show no row for a run that never reached a model.
finding.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/13-c26-end-projects-01a1e904-c8db-71ca-be07-d8530e9.png. The cost_ledger row has kind subscription, model '<synthetic>', USD 0.
finding.repro: Any run on the subscription that Claude Code ends with an error. Here it was a refused sign-in; Claude Code also sends a synthetic message when the plan's limit is reached.
finding.suspected_cause: The SDK driver books the usage of Claude Code's synthetic error message under that message's model field, '<synthetic>'.

verdict.root_cause: When an API call fails (a refused sign-in, or the plan's limit), Claude Code makes up an assistant message itself. That message carries `error` (for example "authentication_failed"), `model: "<synthetic>"` (Claude Code's own constant, present in the bundled binary of @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.304) and an all-zero `usage` object. The SDK driver's assistant branch books any message that has a `usage` object (packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:424-432). R-modelusage takes the model from the message: `const model = typeof m?.model === "string" && m.model ? m.model : req.model`, so the model is "<synthetic>". The driver also adds one to numTurns. book() then calls hooks.afterModelCall with that model (sdk.ts:353-366), and afterModelCall writes a cost_ledger row with `model: opts.model ?? ctx.model` (packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:271). The price lookup for "<synthetic>" fails and falls back to the run model's price, so the cost is 0 and no money is wrong. The daemon's Costs view groups the ledger by its model column and uses the raw key as the label (packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1196-1205). The run facts know no run on "<synthetic>", so Runs shows the entry count of 1 and Accepted shows — (views.ts:1271-1280). The Costs tab then prints "<synthetic> · 1 · — · — · CHF 0.00". The evidence DB (/tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/home/data/state.sqlite) holds exactly that row: kind subscription, model '<synthetic>', all token counts 0, the anthropic-sdk run that failed with "401 OAuth access token is invalid". That run's own model is claude-sonnet-5-5. The Claude Code provider (packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:166-169) skips the error message with `continue`, so only the SDK driver books it. The unit tests missed it because the fake error message in sdk-driver.test.ts:342-346 has no `model` and no `usage`, unlike the real shape. This breaks design §5 rules 3 and 6: an internal marker is shown as a name.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:424-432 (the model taken from the synthetic message and booked); ledger write at packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:271; shown via packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1196-1205 and :1271-1280
verdict.fix_sketch: In SdkAgentDriver.handle's assistant branch, treat Claude Code's synthetic error message as "no model call". When `msg.error` is a string, or `m.model === "<synthetic>"` (one named constant, for example CLAUDE_CODE_SYNTHETIC_MODEL), do not book, do not add to numTurns and do not run the beforeModelCall estimate. Still record sdkError as now. If such a message ever has usage above zero, book it under req.model, never under the marker. To be safe, resultTotals/resultShares should also map a "<synthetic>" key in modelUsage to the run model. Optionally, as defence for rows already in the ledger: the daemon's Costs view (and services/state-api/src/views.ts byModel) could leave out a model bucket whose key is "<synthetic>" and whose usd and tokens are all 0, or fold it into the run's model. Update the fake error messages in sdk-driver.test.ts (rate_limit) and in cred-world/subscription-path to Claude Code's real shape (id, model "<synthetic>", zero usage). Note it in docs/maintainers/runtime.md next to R-modelusage.
